meaning_fixes.after: <sp(20)>Currently in combat with the Siberian Railway.<ab(500)>
meaning_fixes.reason: Orchestrator ruling on the clipped nickname: web search (English Wikipedia, ANN, Bandai dub cast lists, DVD reviews) finds only the full 'Siberian Railroad/Railway' in English King Gainer sources and no clipped form, so the project coinage 'Sibe-Rail' is replaced by the locked glossary name 'Siberian Railway'.

checked_decisions.finding: Clipped Siberian Railway nickname: English Wikipedia uses only 'Siberian Railroad'/'Siberian Railway'; search results from ANN, dub cast lists and DVD reviews likewise show the full name; no clipped English form found anywhere. 'Sibe-Rail' replaced by locked 'Siberian Railway'. The nickname occurs in 16 corpus rows (1905, 2000, 4426, 4432, 4433, 4540, 5902, 5962, 7518, 9626, 9704, 9717, 16665, 16811, 16923, 16962); none of the later ones is translated yet, so this sets the form.
'Gauli Team' kept: Wikipedia uses both 'Gauli Squad' and 'Gauli team'; 'Team' avoids the missing q glyph. The character glossary role text ('Gauli Squad') is descriptive, not a locked term.

Exchange reads as a military ship captain and a subordinate guarding a quoted 'cargo' (content resembles the Eureka Seven military ship tracking the Gekko, but nothing in the table names the speakers). No identities added; 'sortie' in 1917 and the passives in 1920/1922 keep the omitted subjects open. Meaning correct.
'helpers' is an accurate rendering of the casual, honorific-suffixed word for backup/hired help; kept, same word in both rows.
Verb unsaid in source; open-ended 'Why are you...?!' is correct.
Object 'him' with omitted verb; 'why bring him along' is supported by the reply in 1915 (got him caught up in it). Accepted as inference, see uncertainties.
Harsh second-person line kept speaker-neutral; meaning (a name and nothing behind it) correct.
Source is a bare 'found!'. It follows the enemy discovery lines 1942-1945, so the train being spotted is the right reading; 'It's been spotted' keeps it loose.
Side not determinable from the table (follows the enemy all-out-attack call, precedes the time-running-out lines). Neutral wording kept; nothing side-specific added.
Rebuke target unstated in Japanese; English needs a pronoun and 'you' is the natural failure-line reading. Kept, flagged.
Banter kept identity-free; the split sentence 1963/1964 joins correctly (scatter bullets, not lives).
1967/1969 speaker is Renton (Eureka beside him); partner unidentified; no gender supplied for the partner.
'We left the military' is Gekkostate-side; translation is speaker-neutral and correct. 1972 'had a run-in' = fought each other once, confirmed by 1975-1976 (who won / a draw).
'high priest' for the senior-cleric term versus plain 'priest' for the casual word in 2018/2026: the distinction matches the source.

uncertainties.issue: Replacing the nickname with the full name loses the casual clipping. If the orchestrator prefers a short form, 'the Railway' would be the natural English clipping, but it is not attested either; whichever is chosen must be applied to all 16 rows listed in checked_decisions.
batch_01895_glossary_proposals.json still proposes 'Sibe-Rail'; not edited (outside the batch/review files I was allowed to touch). It should be withdrawn.
Verb inferred ('bring him along'); an equally possible reading is 'why is he with you / in that machine'. Both fit 1915.

Whether the captain is asked not to sortie personally or not to launch the ship's forces is not settled; 1920 (KLF forces will be sent out anyway) slightly favours 'do not launch'. 'sortie' covers both. 1920 'unit' could equally be plural.
What Gainer must hurry with is unstated (getting the Overman moving, judging by 1925-1931); left unstated in English too.
'you' supplied where the source has no addressee.
